method: 100 plain GCC compilations and one warmup per fresh guest, CPU2, icount0. Same original fork source/build flags except the recorded diagnostic full-flush condition. The fork arms have x-capstone-u-mode=true on virt without native kernel flags.
conclusion: Restoring conservative full SFENCE.VMA flushing makes the U-mode fork slower than upstream. The existing page-specific path reduces host CPU by 37.25% forward and 37.55% reverse; it explains the fork platform/plain advantage despite its other overheads. This optimization already exists in the native handoff baseline.
profiles: host-configuration-qualification.json identifies the separate 500-compilation profiles and their evidence archive; upstream has substantially more MMU refill and jump-cache-clear self cost.
limits: Host speed shifted substantially between forward and reverse cohorts; report both directions rather than comparing absolute times to earlier campaigns.
The stock/full difference is not attributed further by this experiment.
No security checks or production source changed. Full flushing is conservative but deliberately fails the fixture that pins page-specific behavior.
Exact output regression against the same reference, not hardware performance or a SPEC score.
